output.title: Attribution starts with one source field you can trust
output.body:
If you are measuring attribution, the first question is not which dashboard to buy. It is whether your leads already pass through one place where source can be recorded cleanly. If the answer is no, attribution is a data-plumbing problem first, and an AI problem later.

For a small business, that usually means one workflow: website form, email reply, CRM entry, or sales record. Ask this simple check: when a lead becomes a customer, can you trace it back to one channel or campaign without guessing? If the answer depends on memory, a spreadsheet note, or whatever someone typed last Tuesday, the measurement is already shaky.

The next step is a small manual spot-check. Pick a recent sample of closed deals, look up the original source trail, and compare it with what your CRM or tracking field says. The sample does not prove the whole system is right or wrong. It just tells you whether the control is real or decorative.

If the source field is blank, inconsistent, or routinely overwritten, fix the input rule before adding AI. Once source data is reliable, then you can decide whether lead scoring, channel-based replies, or another automation is worth testing. Before that, the model would only help you measure noise more neatly.
